bears.name: Chicago Bears
bears.summary: The Chicago Bears improved to 7-2 after surviving a wild Week 9 game, edging the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 27-24 on a game-winning field goal despite quarterback Caleb Williams throwing a career-high four interceptions. At 7-2, the Bears are a half game behind the Minnesota Vikings for the NFC North lead.

lions.name: Detroit Lions
lions.summary: The biggest story coming out of Detroit is that the Lions stood pat at Monday's NFL trade deadline after acquiring safety Andre Cisco from the Jets the day before, as the Detroit Lions announced a roster move after the trade for safety Andre Cisco was officially confirmed, and elected not to make another move on trade deadline day after making one the day prior . The move addresses depth at safety while Kerby Joseph continues working back from a knee injury, and comes on the heels of Detroit's 19-9 win over Miami that improved their record to 6-2, as the Lions acquired Andre Cisco in a trade with the New York Jets while Kerby Joseph works his way back from a knee injury, with the defense earning respect after the win over Miami .

packers.name: Green Bay Packers
packers.summary: The Green Bay Packers stood pat at the NFL trade deadline, reportedly missing out on both Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor and defensive lineman Grover Stewart after talks stalled. Reportedly, the Packers had an offer on the table for Colts defensive lineman Grover Stewart, but Indianapolis dragged its feet and Green Bay moved on, content to stand pat with what they have.

vikings.name: Minnesota Vikings
vikings.summary: The Minnesota Vikings made the biggest splash of the day by trading for quarterback Kirk Cousins, striking a deal with the Raiders to bring Cousins back to Minnesota in exchange for the team's third-round pick in 2027 . The move comes after Carson Wentz crashed and burned during a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 9, prompting the Vikings to make getting another quarterback their top priority heading into the trade deadline .
